page_title: Glass: your computer, in any browser

sources.entry: Glass - Low-latency remote desktop for Mac and Linux that you view from any browser, with nothing to install on the viewing device. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Ntarasiuk/glass) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Glass
summary.one_liner: Glass is a free, open-source remote desktop that lets you control a Mac or Linux computer from any browser, such as an iPad, phone, or laptop, with about 20 ms of latency.
use_cases: Control a home Mac or Linux computer from an iPad or phone
Give remote tech support to someone with nothing installed
Use an iPad as a second screen for a Mac
Access your own computers over a private Tailscale network
Supervise an AI agent operating your computer
Check status and updates across several of your computers
summary.what_it_does: Glass runs on a Mac or Linux computer and streams its screen to any modern browser on another device, with the page stating about 20 ms of delay and up to 120 fps. Access can be set up over a Tailscale tailnet, where the computer is reached at a private address without opening ports, or via a one-time end-to-end encrypted link made with glass link --anywhere. For support, the other person runs a one-line install and reads out a nine-digit code, and they must approve the session before it starts. The page also describes a signed-in view of multiple computers showing online status, disk, FileVault, firewall and version, plus microphone, sound, file, and clipboard sharing, and an iPad mode that can extend the Mac desktop with Apple Pencil pressure. Installation is via a curl command piped to sh.
notable: Viewable from any browser, with nothing to install on the viewing device
Works over Tailscale or a one-time end-to-end encrypted link, with no ports opened
Quick support mode using a nine-digit code and explicit approval before the helper sees the screen
Apple Pencil pressure support for using an iPad as a second display
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or later on the computer being controlled
Team features such as single sign-on, access rules, and console are listed but their pricing is not stated
Tailscale is needed on both computer and device for the tailnet method, unless using the one-time link
